title: Active learning guides a tested ternary hydrogen-evolution catalyst
summary: Gaussian-process active learning guided nanoparticle experiments using metal-precursor ratios. A Pt0.65Ru0.30Ni0.05 precursor mixture yielded a catalyst requiring 54.2 millivolts overpotential at 20 milliamperes per square centimetre, versus 68.2 for similarly prepared platinum. The final particles differed from the precursor composition. This laboratory result does not establish commercial electrolyzer performance.
organization: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology; Seoul National University; Harvard University; Kookmin University

evidence.tested: Iteratively selected catalysts underwent synthesis, microscopy, elemental characterization and acidic-electrolyte hydrogen-evolution measurements against same-method comparators.
evidence.unknown: The precursor ratio is not the measured particle stoichiometry. Independent replication, commercial durability and broad model generalization remain unestablished.
evidence.ai_role: A Gaussian process maps eight-component precursor fractions to overpotential; uncertainty and predicted performance guide experiments whose measurements update the model.

source_review.scope: Author-deposited primary full Methods/results through indexed PDF, exact front identity, publisher online date and current PubMed notice metadata.
